{{Quote|While curiosity is not a standard Givin trait, I consider it good business to know what I transport.|Elis Helrot|<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run">{{WEGCite|story=Running the Sisar|book=Secrets of the Sisar Run}}</ref>}}
'''Elis Helrot''' was a [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] who worked as a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]], [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]], and [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] trader during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. A native of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]], he possessed an analytical mind and was considered a ruthless and unscrupulous businessman by others. Helrot operated from his personally modified [[Starship/Legends|starship]], the ''[[Hinthra]]'', and often made slaving and [[Spice/Legends|spice]] runs from the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] world of Tatooine to the planets [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] and [[Pavilion port|Pavilion]]. A longstanding feud developed between Helrot and the [[Morseerian/Legends|Morseerian]] smuggler [[Nabrun Leids/Legends|Nabrun Leids]] during the Givin's career. Both were in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] on Tatooine one day in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] when the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and the smuggler [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] were involved in separate skirmishes with other [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] denizens.

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Helrot and the crew of the ''Hinthra'' took part in a competition organized by [[Mal Biron]], a [[Vigo/Legends|Vigo]] of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] criminal organization who hoped to discover new and loyal allies. The ''Hinthra'' was one of seven smuggling vessels that moved along the [[Sisar Run/Legends|Sisar Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] in a race to deliver secret cargo to the [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury liner]] ''[[Destination: Adventure!]]''. When he received his cargo at the [[Nwarcol Point]] [[Space station/Legends|space station]], Helrot opened its sealed container and found unarmed [[Mag-pulse warhead/Legends|magnetic pulse warhead]] inside. He smelled profit and, after arriving at the ''Destination: Adventure!'', offered 10,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to another smuggling crew for their identical cargo. The conversation was overheard by Biron, whose enforcers responded by [[Stun/Legends|stunning]] Helrot and his crew into [[Sleep/Legends|unconsciousness]].

==Biography==
===Time on Tatooine===
{{Quote|The ghoulish one is a Givin.|Feltipern Trevagg, describing Elis Helrot to M'iiyoom Onith|<ref name="Audio">[[Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale (audio drama)|"Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale" audio drama]]</ref>}}
[[File:Elisincantina.jpg|thumb|left|165px|Elis Helrot, inside Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]]
A [[Givin/Legends|Givin]], Elis Helrot hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]],<ref name="Hasbro" /> his [[Species/Legends|species]]' [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="Ultimate Alien Anthology" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], he was active as a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]],<ref name="Inside the Worlds">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]],<ref name="JKTCG">{{JKTCG|set=Premiere|cardname=Elis Helrot • Givin Merchant|link=http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/cardlists/premier/large/13Uelishelrot.html}}</ref> and [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] trader.<ref name="Hasbro" /> Helrot operated out of his [[Starship/Legends|starship]], the ''[[Hinthra]]'', a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]]<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" /> that he himself heavily modified. He often transported slaves and [[Spice/Legends|spice]] to [[Kala'uun/Legends|Kala'uun]],<ref name="ccg" /> a [[City/Legends|city]] on the planet [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]],<ref name="Platt's Starport Guide">''[[Platt's Starport Guide]]''</ref> as well as to the planet [[Pavilion port|Pavilion]].<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" /> Over the course of his career, Helrot developed a rivalry with the [[Morseerian/Legends|Morseerian]] smuggler [[Nabrun Leids/Legends|Nabrun Leids]].<ref name="Leids">{{JKTCG|set=Scum and Villainy|cardname=Nabrun Leids • Fringe Smuggler|link=http://www.cambiacartas.com/img/cards/jedi-knights/761/big/63L.jpg}}</ref> During the war, Helrot was often on the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] world of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], scouring the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] for information on slaves and spice that needed transport<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|33|Helrot, Elis}}</ref> and spending [[Time/Legends|time]] at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]].<ref name="Hasbro" /> He frequently collected cargo on the desert planet and made many deliveries from Tatooine to Ryloth.<ref name="ccg" />

On a day in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Helrot was in [[Chalmun/Legends|Chalmun's]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] concurrently with a number of other smugglers and criminals, including Nabrun Leids.<ref name="Inside the Worlds" /> The Givin played a card game with the [[Abyssin/Legends|Abyssin]] [[Myo/Legends|Myo]] and the [[Talz/Legends|Talz]] [[Muftak/Legends|Muftak]],<ref name="Nightlily">{{StoryCite|story=Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> but he eventually left the game and sat down at a booth with the [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]] [[Feltipern Trevagg/Legends|Feltipern Trevagg]] and the [[H'nemthe (species)/Legends|H'nemthe]] [[M'iiyoom Onith/Legends|M'iiyoom Onith]].<ref name="Databank">{{DB|species|givin|Givin}}</ref> The two were preoccupied with discussing a forthcoming sexual encounter and paid him little mind. The [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] entered the cantina shortly thereafter and was harassed by the [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]] and [[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]]. When it escalated into a physical encounter, Onith grew frightened, and she and Trevagg left the establishment.<ref name="Audio" /> Helrot was then joined by the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] [[Ohwun De Maal/Legends|Ohwun De Maal]], and the pair were speaking when the smuggler [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] shot and [[Death/Legends|killed]] the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]] at a nearby table.<ref name="A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

===Running the Sisar===
{{Quote|The ''Hinthra''{{'s}} not going anywhere. Elis has a lot of explaining to do.|Kalend Thora, after the stunning of Helrot and his crew|<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />}}
[[File:Squishyhelrot.jpg|thumb|right|Helrot inside Docking Bay 42]]
In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Helrot and his crew of three aboard the ''Hinthra''&mdash;[[Unidentified Givin 1|two]] [[Unidentified Givin 2|other]] Givins and a [[Unidentified Human (Hinthra)|Human male]]&mdash;were invited to the planet [[Sriluur/Legends|Sriluur's]] [[Meirm City]] by the [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] smuggler [[Mal Biron]], who was seeking out competent and trustworthy allies. Helrot heeded the call and took the ''Hinthra'' to Sriluur, where the ship's crew touched down and, following instructions sent to their [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] by Biron, made their way to Meirm City's [[Docking Bay 42 (Sriluur)|Docking Bay 42]]. Therein, they joined a larger group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] who had all been invited; Nabrun Leids was among those present. A [[Service droid/Legends|droid]] served the motley crew food and drinks, and they ate an uncomfortably silent lunch as they waited for Biron to arrive. During the meal, Biron's Duros assistant, [[Kalend Thora]], surveyed the [[Captain/Legends|captains]] present and recorded their identities. Biron eventually descended the [[Entry ramp/Legends|boarding ramp]] of his docked freighter, the ''[[Eyeshine]]'', and with little preamble told the smugglers what he had planned for them.<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />

The Shistavenan claimed that he needed important cargo moved along the [[Sisar Run/Legends|Sisar Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]], and that he had assembled the diverse group to ensure at least some of it arrived at its destination. 5,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] would be paid to each crew for making the Sisar Run, with an additional 5,000 awarded to the first crew to deliver their payload. The crews were to make their way to a secret location to receive their cargo before moving to the [[Salin Corridor/Legends|Salin Corridor]] and rendezvousing with the [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury liner]] ''[[Destination: Adventure!]]'', where they would drop off their load. With his instructions complete, Biron greeted each of the crews in turn. None of them were aware that he was a [[Vigo/Legends|Vigo]] of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] criminal organization, or that the forthcoming task was in fact a test of their skills and loyalty in preparation for a larger operation that he had planned. Helrot and his crew returned to the ''Hinthra'' and plugged their datapad into the ship's [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]]. A secret file of Biron's then opened and revealed their first destination: the [[Novolek Beacon/Legends|Novolek Beacon]], a [[Neutron star/Legends|neutron star]] in the [[Periphery/Legends|Periphery]] region of [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />

The ''Hinthra'' arrived at the beacon around the same [[Time/Legends|time]] as the six other smuggling vessels it faced. Helrot received a signal from a nearby [[communications satellite]], but the neutron [[Star/Legends|star's]] presence was disrupting the signal, and the gathered starships raced to the [[Satellite/Legends|satellite]], all vying for the opportunity to be the first to discover their next destination. It was [[Nwarcol Point]], a refueling [[Space station/Legends|station]] located at the intersection of the Sisar Run and the Salin Corridor, and after intercepting the satellite's signal, Helrot and his crew fled into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. They soon after arrived and docked at Nwarcol, where they were informed by Biron's datapad file that the coordinates for ''Destination: Adventure!'' would be provided to them in thirty [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]]. They located their cargo aboard the station within that time and loaded it aboard the ''Hinthra''; although it was sealed inside a cargo pod, Helrot peeked inside and discovered that the cargo consisted of several unarmed [[Mag-pulse warhead|magnetic pulse warheads]].<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />

[[File:Helrotsdeal.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Helrot makes an offer to another smuggling crew.]]
When they received their next coordinates, Helrot and his crew traveled along the Salin Corridor toward the luxury liner and emerged from hyperspace concurrently with their opponents&mdash;the race remained tight. An [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] patrol that consisted of six [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] and a [[Guardian-class light cruiser|''Guardian''-class light cruiser]] stood between the smugglers and their destination, but when three pirate ships emerged from hyperspace behind the smugglers, the Imperials, who were being paid off by Black Sun, allowed the smugglers to pass and [[Battle of the Destination: Adventure!|engaged]] the pirates. The ''Hinthra'' was not the first ship to arrive, but Biron nevertheless greeted Helrot and his crew after they docked. He then awarded the winning crew 5,000 credits and suggested that everyone retire to the luxury liner's lounge for free food and drinks. Once there, Helrot approached the winning crew and invited them into a back hallway, where he told them what he had seen inside the cargo pod. Helrot had calculated the value of a completed [[Warhead/Legends|warhead]] to be a high price and offered 10,000 credits for the other crew's cargo, so that he might arm the weapons himself and reap the consequent profits.<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />

{{RPG|"[[Running the Sisar]]"}}
The smugglers declined his offer, but Helrot and his crew nonetheless made their way to the luxury liner's cargo area. There, they discovered that the cargo had been taken to the ''Destination: Adventure!''{{'s}} galley, where they found it being loaded into a large freezer. Before the group could enter the freezer, they were ambushed by Biron and his enforcers, who had overheard Helrot's earlier conversation via planted [[Listening device/Legends|listening devices]]. Biron's enforcers fired [[Stun/Legends|stun]] bolts at Helrot and his crew and knocked them [[Sleep/Legends|unconscious]]. Kalend Thora then announced that the traitors would be interrogated.<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I opened the cargo pod, and must say, I was impressed by what I saw. It takes a lot to impress a Givin.|Elis Helrot|<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />}}
[[File:Ruthlessandairtight.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Elis Helrot: ruthless and airtight]]
A smuggler,<ref name="Inside the Worlds" /> merchant,<ref name="JKTCG" /> and slaver,<ref name="Hasbro" /> Elis Helrot was considered by others to be an unscrupulous individual<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" /> with ruthless and airtight business practices.<ref name="JKTCG" /> He regularly scoured Mos Eisley in search of slaves to be transported,<ref name="CSWE" /> and, while working for Mal Biron, he was prepared to betray the Shistavenan in order to make a handsome profit.<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" /> During his smuggling career, Helrot was involved in a longstanding feud with rival smuggler Nabrun Leids.<ref name="Leids" /> Possessed of an analytical mind, he was not easily impressed and was solely concerned with a situation's bottom line. Helrot disliked being ignorant of the contents of any cargo that he transported<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" /> and was willing to beg, borrow, or steal a weapon if he required its use.<ref name="Hasbro" />

Helrot was an able pilot<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" /> and also showed prowess as a [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]], having made a number of modifications to his ship, the ''Hinthra''.<ref name="ccg" /> Like all members of his species,<ref name="Ultimate Alien Anthology" /> he revered mathematics. Solving numerical puzzles was one of his favorite pastimes. Another trait that Helrot shared with all Givin was the ability to seal his [[exoskeleton]] and survive exposure to the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of space.<ref name="Hasbro" /> The [[Color/Legends|white]] and [[Hair/Legends|hairless]] exoskeleton included a pair of sunken black [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="ccg" /> Feltipern Trevagg found Helrot to be "ghoulish" in appearance.<ref name="Audio" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Another booth-based reshoot alien, this walking skeleton with the anguished face was based on original illustrations by Ralph McQuarrie. It was nicknamed "Skull Head," and was to have the proper name of Kull.|Author [[Pablo Hidalgo]], discussing the creation of Elis Helrot|<ref name="Aliases">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref>}}
The character who would eventually be known as Elis Helrot<ref name="ccg" /> was created to be a background character in the cantina scene of the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']], later renamed ''A New Hope''.<ref name="Databank" /> The character's rubber mask was constructed by makeup artist [[Rick Baker]],<ref name="Beastmaster">{{InsiderCite|126|The Beastmaster!}}</ref> whose design was based on concept art by artist [[Ralph McQuarrie]].<ref name="Aliases" /> The mask was worn by an uncredited extra during supplemental shooting for the cantina scene, which was filmed during the movie's post-production when director [[George Lucas]] decided to liven the scene with more action and additional characters.<ref name="Beastmaster" />

The alien was nicknamed "Skull Head" on-set and was going to officially be named "Kull," but the idea was ultimately abandoned.<ref name="Aliases" /> During filming, "Skull Head" sat in a booth with two characters<ref name="Databank" /> who would later be christened M'iiyoom Onith and Feltipern Trevagg,<ref name="Nightlily" /> but only the two of them are clearly visible on-screen in the final cut of the film. The back of Helrot's head does appear later in the cantina scene, however, visible behind a seated Greedo.<ref name="A New Hope" /> Set photos of Helrot at the table with Onith and Trevagg later appeared in several [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] sources.<ref name="Storybook">''[[The Star Wars Storybook]]''</ref><ref name="Poster Monthly">[[Star Wars Official Poster Monthly 16|''Star Wars Official Poster Monthly'' 16]]</ref><ref name="Galaxy Guide 7">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref>

[[File:Bakerandfriends.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Rick Baker and his team amidst the masks of Helrot and various other Cantina denizens]]
The name "Elis Helrot" was developed for the [[1995]] release of the [[Decipher]] [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]]{{'s}} ''[[Premiere Limited]]'' set.<ref name="ccg" /> Helrot has additionally been mentioned in several sourcebooks and encyclopedias,<ref name="Ultimate Alien Anthology" /><ref name="Inside the Worlds" /><ref name="CSWE" /> as well as in [[2001]]'s [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]], which established a rivalry between Helrot and Nabrun Leids,<ref name="Leids" /> another character from ''A New Hope''{{'s}} cantina scene.<ref name="A New Hope" /> During gameplay, playing a Helrot or a Leids card against the other will force either one or both of the cards to be discarded.<ref name="JKTCG" /><ref name="Leids" /><ref name="JK2">{{JKTCG|set=Scum and Villainy|cardname=Elis Helrot • Underworld Smuggler|link=http://www.cambiacartas.com/img/cards/jedi-knights/761/big/33L.jpg}}</ref><ref name="Leids 2">{{JKTCG|set=Premiere|cardname=Nabrun Leids • Morseerian Transport Expert|link=http://www.cambiacartas.com/img/cards/jedi-knights/760/big/120L.jpg}}</ref> In [[2007]], a 3 ¾ inch action figure of Helrot was released by [[Hasbro]] as part of its ''[[Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection]]'' toy line.<ref name="Hasbro" />

''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]'', a [[1997]] sourcebook designed to supplement [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'', includes Helrot as a non-playable character in the adventure ''[[Running the Sisar]]'', which fleshes out his character and allows the players opportunities to interact with him. Several aspects of Helrot's role in the adventure depend on choices made by both the players and the [[Wikipedia:Gamemaster|gamemaster]]. When the smugglers journey to Novolek Beacon, the ''Hinthra'' is definitely one of the first five ships to arrive, and it is among the top four if the player characters experience a slow journey. During the race to the communications satellite, the beacon will be fired upon by the treacherous [[Az-Iban]] if the gamemaster designates him the first to arrive. If Az-Iban succeeds in destroying it, the [[Quor'sav/Legends|Quor'sav]] [[Kal'Falnl C'ndros]] will intercept the signal in time and share it with the others, including Helrot, for a fee.<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />

As the adventure dictates that the player characters be the first to deliver their payload, the gamemaster is encouraged to establish that any ships which arrive at the ''Destination: Adventure!'' ahead of the players&mdash;possibly including the ''Hinthra''&mdash;are fired upon and damaged by the pirates, thus allowing the players to overtake them. When Helrot later attempts to strike a deal with the player characters, they have the option to accept his offer, in which case they stumble into Biron's trap alongside Helrot and his crew. Such a scenario prevents the players from successfully completing the adventure, and as such, this article assumes that they decline.<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run" />

[[File:Freelygivindrunkdrivingadvice.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Elis Helrot in a 1979 drunk-driving PSA]]
In addition to his canonical appearances, Helrot makes a brief cameo in the [[Infinities|non-canon]] story "[[The Emperor's Court]]," which is included in the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Star Wars Tales 14|''Star Wars Tales'' 14]]. In the story, he is among the various denizens of the Mos Eisley Cantina who attend a trial of Han Solo, accused of shooting first in his murder of Greedo. Helrot and the other spectators watch as Solo and [[Neela|Greedo's mother]] present evidence respectively based on the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] and the original, unaltered version of ''A New Hope''.<ref name="Court">{{Tales|14|The Emperor's Court}}</ref>

Onith is absent in some of ''A New Hope''{{'s}} adaptations&mdash;the cover of ''[[The Mos Eisley Cantina Pop-Up Book]]'' depicts Onith and Trevagg as being seated with Muftak instead of with Helrot, and its interior shows Onith sitting with Greedo and Ponda Baba.<ref name="pop up">''[[The Mos Eisley Cantina Pop-Up Book]]''</ref> However, Helrot does appear, wearing a different outfit than in ''A New Hope'', in a [[1979]] [[Star Friends|drunk-driving PSA]] set in the Mos Eisley Cantina.<ref name="Don't drive drunk">{{SWArchive|url=video/view/000069.html|text=Drunk Driving PSA}}</ref>
